subject: Post-demo: GDPR routing, DPA & SCC module decision + security questionnaire
summary: Post-demo follow-up focused on GDPR contracting path: customer asked which SCC module to apply and whether Redwood will act as processor. Marcus provided recap, SOC 2 attestation, draft DPA and vendor questionnaire; legal (Neha) confirmed Redwood will accept processor role and will produce a redline within 3 business days. Next asks: Lumen to return completed questionnaire and a simple dataflow diagram; target sign by end of month.
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Park <amy@lumenhealth.com>, security@lumenhealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap — GDPR routing, DPA draft & next steps

Hi Amy / Lumen security team,

Thanks for the time today — appreciate the clear questions on privacy and contract routing. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the path to contract: 

Recap from our call:
- Lumen is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing insights and embedding workflows that will include hashed identifiers and short-lived session data.
- Primary compliance asks: SOC 2 Type II evidence, DPA signing, and selection of the appropriate SCC module for EU data.

What we’re sending you now (attached):
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024_Attestation.pdf (attestation, control summary)
- Redwood_DPA_Draft_Lumen_2025.docx (starting draft DPA with standard SCC module options called out)
- Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-Redwood.pdf (blanked answers + owner fields)

Notes on SCC module options and our recommendation:
- Typical mapping for SaaS inference: Lumen = Controller, Redwood = Processor.
- If Lumen prefers specific SCC modules for additional contractual language (e.g., Module 2 processor path vs Module 1 controller path), we can accept Module 2 as the default processor route.

Immediate asks for Lumen (requested by next Wednesday, 25 Jun):
1) Confirm which SCC module you prefer (if you have a legal preference).
2) Return the completed vendor questionnaire (we attached a Redwood version; feel free to send your questionnaire and we’ll populate answers).
3) A very short dataflow diagram (PDF or PNG) showing what data leaves Lumen and what stays in-session — this helps our legal team map the DPA clauses.

Internal note: looping in Laura (ops) for SOC/attestation questions and Neha (legal) for DPA/SCC module redline.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick follow-up with procurement/legal if useful.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0148

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2024_Attestation.pdf; Redwood_DPA_Draft_Lumen_2025.docx; Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-Redwood.pdf

From: Amy Park <amy@lumenhealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@lumenhealth.com, procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — GDPR routing, DPA draft & next steps

Hi Marcus — thanks for the recap and for sending the materials. Quick answers from our side: 

- SOC 2: good to have the attestation; our InfoSec will review and may follow up with a short control question set.
- SCC preference: Lumen typically routes to the Module 2 (Processor addendum) when we remain the Controller, so that sounds fine — we need to confirm with legal but provisional preference is Module 2.
- Controller/Processor: Lumen will be Controller; we expect Redwood to be Processor for the services described.

I attached our completed vendor questionnaire (Lumen_Vendor_Q_FINAL.docx) — it's got a few specific questions around data retention for embeddings and cross-border access for support staff. Could you have legal ops confirm answers for those sections?

Two clarifying questions for you: 
1) For the DPA draft, will Redwood accept our requested SCC module (Module 2) and the standard EU addendum?
2) We asked about SOC 2 monitoring: do you have a public status page or one-pager that highlights control ownership for incident response and access controls?

If all looks good, procurement wants to get a redline DPA and the questionnaire answers back by EOW (next Friday, 27 Jun).

Thanks — Amy
Amy Park
Sr. PM, Data Platforms | LumenHealth
amy@lumenhealth.com

Attachments: Lumen_Vendor_Q_FINAL.docx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Park <amy@lumenhealth.com>, security@lumenhealth.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap — GDPR routing, DPA draft & next steps

Hi Amy — appreciate the rapid turnaround and the questionnaire. Quick answers inline and proposed timeline: 

- SCC Module: We can accept Module 2 (Processor) with the standard EU addendum when Lumen is Controller. That matches our standard routing and is what our legal team expects for this class of work.

- DPA & data retention: Our draft DPA (attached) includes a retention table and support for short-lived embeddings (we typically default to 30 days for derived embeddings unless agreed otherwise). If you need a 0-day/no-store option we can discuss scope and implications — that may affect feature availability and cost.

- SOC 2 visibility: public attestation is attached. For a compact control mapping (incident response / access controls) see the attestation appendix pages 6–8. We do also maintain an internal status page, which I’ve shared below for your InfoSec team: https://drive.redwood.ai/attestations/Redwood_SOC2_2024.pdf

Proposed timeline from Redwood: 
- Today: internal legal reviews your questionnaire and the SCC request.
- +3 business days: Neha will push a redline DPA back to this thread (we aim Wed 25 Jun).
- By EOW (27 Jun): we’ll aim to have questionnaire answers and a preliminary redline DPA.

Neha / Laura — can you confirm the redline timeline and if you need any extra info from Lumen on the dataflow? 

Marcus

Hi Amy / Marcus — looping in legal to confirm next steps. Short update: 

1) Redwood legal confirms we accept the Processor role (Lumen as Controller) for the services described. That aligns with Module 2 routing.
2) We will produce a redline of the attached DPA and call out the SCC Module 2 (Processor) as the path forward — redline target: EOB Wed, 25 Jun (3 business days).
3) For the few questionnaire items flagged (embeddings retention, cross-border support), Laura from Ops will provide the operational answers; if Lumen can provide a simple dataflow diagram (even a single slide) it will speed the mapping and final sign-off.

If you want a short calibration call between our privacy team and Lumen legal/security, please propose times next week and we’ll join.
